description:
**`ROADMAP.md` documents the `77`–`92` era and is silent on roughly 60% of the merged program.** Audited 2026-08-25 against disk.

Its banner reads *"Shipping & self-hosting (v0.8.0 — see VERSION)"*; `VERSION` is `0.8.94`. Line 55 says *"1/1 built-program tasklists merged (`77`); 15 proposed forward tasklists authored … the runnable head is the agent-output quality & alignment band (`88`–`91`)"* — that band shipped between 08-12 and 08-18. Line 153 says *"remaining work is hardening and breadth … numbered from the current max, `77`."* `77` stopped being the max on 2026-08-01.

**Bands `93`–`113` do not appear in the file at all.** A grep for `9[3-9]|1[01][0-9]` returns nothing; the highest number present is `92`. Concept greps for `chief usage`, `chief decide`, `chief status`, `machine-wide` and `iteration-outcome` all return zero. The CLI roster at line 20 lists twelve subcommands; `bin/chief` dispatches eight more (`status · lint · gen · events · usage · quality · approve · decide`).

**Two coherent programmes are missing, and they deserve naming rather than a list of numbers.** `104`–`109` are OPERATOR ERGONOMICS — usage reporting, decision tasklists, list/ps, machine-wide concurrency. `110`–`113` are one thesis, *chief learning to tell real progress from motion*: a green branch verified three times, a 529 misread as a usage wall, a bookkeeping commit scored as progress, a story that may terminate false. That is an ITERATION-OUTCOME TAXONOMY and the roadmap has no vocabulary for it.

**The mechanism is on the record inside this repo.** `86-doc-sync-gate` shipped and `test/doc-sync.sh` enforces README ↔ VERSION ↔ subcommand parity — and does not cover `ROADMAP.md`. That is precisely why `README.md:347` correctly says `v0.8.94` while the roadmap says `v0.8.0`. Fixing the text without closing that gap re-runs this audit in a fortnight; the measured portfolio drift rate is about two weeks.
warmup: grep -n 'Last updated\|v0\.8\.0' ROADMAP.md | head -5; cat VERSION
ls tasks/chief/completed/ | sed 's/-.*//' | sort -n | uniq | tail -25 | tr '\n' ' '
grep -n 'ROADMAP' test/doc-sync.sh || echo 'ROADMAP.md is NOT covered by the doc-sync gate'

userStories.title: The roadmap states what is true today
acceptanceCriteria: The banner, the Current State block and every phase row are rewritten against `tasks/chief/completed/`. All 35 records carry a real `mergedToMain` — verify rather than assume, and cite shas for the bands you mark done.
The version claim is derived from `VERSION`, not restated. A roadmap asserting `v0.8.0` beside a `VERSION` of `0.8.94` is the specific failure this tasklist exists to end.
The CLI roster matches `bin/chief`'s dispatch table. Eight subcommands are currently missing from it.
Internal contradictions are resolved: the file currently says five first-class providers in one place, four in another and three in a third. Pick the true one and state it once.
userStories.notes: Rewrote banner, Current State, and every existing phase row against tasks/chief/completed/. All 37 records carry a real mergedToMain (0 MISSING); shas resolve bd030a6 (77, 2026-08-01) .. 716c9e4 (113, 2026-08-26). Version claim now bold **v0.9.1** == VERSION 0.9.1 (was v0.8.0). CLI roster 12 -> 22. Provider contradiction resolved to five first-class. check-doc-links: 0 dead vs 0 on main; test/doc-sync.sh PASS; chief lint clean.

userStories.title: The two unnamed programmes get names and rows
acceptanceCriteria: `104`–`109` are recorded as a coherent OPERATOR ERGONOMICS phase, not as a list of merged numbers.

`110`–`113` are recorded as one thesis about iteration-outcome honesty, with the measurement behind each: three verifies of an already-green branch; a 529 Overloaded slept on as a usage wall; five bookkeeping commits scoring as progress and stretching a 5-iteration budget to 11; a story re-driven 63 commits whose right answer was `passes:false`.
The `93`–`103` band is placed too — merge safety, worktree reaping, `chief status`, reap orphanhood. Roughly 21 merged tasklists are currently invisible.
`docs/decisions/conflict-predictor-adoption-decision.md` and the two active tasklists are reflected, so the 'Loose wishlist — Empty. No future threads are parked' line stops being false.
userStories.notes: Added three named phase sections to ROADMAP.md: 'Operating the fleet' (93-103, 11 rows), 'Operator ergonomics' (104-109, 6 rows) and 'Iteration-outcome honesty' (110-113, 4 rows, stated as one thesis with each measurement: ~34min to merge an already-green 4/4 branch and 2 merge-phase verifies over 6 iterations on a 3/3; three iterations of API Error 529 hitting stall 3/2 with 2,029 files intact on disk; five re-check-stamp commits stretching a 5-iteration budget to 11 over 1h32m; 63 commits / 21 iterations in one run / 42 identical measurements on a story whose right answer was passes:false). Replaced the false 'Loose wishlist - Empty' block with 'In flight' (114/115/116) + 'Open threads' citing docs/decisions/conflict-predictor-adoption-decision.md. VERIFIED: all 37 completed/ stems AND all 37 mergedToMain shas now appear in ROADMAP.md (0 missing, checked by loop); 3/3 live tasklists referenced. Gates: check-doc-links --ratchet 0 dead vs 0 on main; test/doc-sync.sh DOC-SYNC PASS; chief lint 3 tasklists clean. File 274 -> 360 lines.

userStories.title: The gate that would have caught this covers the file
acceptanceCriteria: `test/doc-sync.sh` is extended to cover `ROADMAP.md`. At minimum it fails when the roadmap's stated version disagrees with `VERSION`, and when a tasklist stem in `completed/` is absent from the roadmap — the two checks that would each independently have caught this drift.
The check is cheap and offline, in keeping with the gate it joins. It must not require a network call or a model.

It is proven able to FAIL: a negative-control fixture drives it red, in the same shape the rest of this repo's guards use. A gate nobody has watched fail is indistinguishable from one that always passes.
The rationale is recorded where the next reader looks: this repo shipped a doc-sync gate that deliberately did not cover the roadmap, and the roadmap is the file that rotted.
userStories.notes: test/doc-sync.sh extended to cover ROADMAP.md with the two checks that would each independently have caught the audited drift: the roadmap's bold **vX.Y.Z** == VERSION (shared with README via version_claims_ok), and every merged stem in tasks/chief/completed/ named in ROADMAP.md. Green: 'DOC-SYNC PASS - README and ROADMAP state v0.9.2; README documents every bin/chief subcommand; ROADMAP names all 37 merged tasklists' (exit 0). PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL - 4 negative self-checks now run inline (2 README + 2 new ROADMAP) and all trip; driven red by hand too, reproducing both halves of the 2026-08-25 audit: a ROADMAP claiming **v0.8.0** beside VERSION 0.9.1 -> exit 1, and a ROADMAP stripped of '99-reap-must-not-infer-orphanhood' -> exit 1. Offline: grep/sed/awk/basename over tracked files, no network, no model. Gates: bash -n all 60 shell files clean; shellcheck -S error clean on test/doc-sync.sh + .chief/verify.sh (v0.11.0 via npx - the 3 errors it reports in engine/quality.sh:60 and engine/sweep.sh:396,404 are byte-identical on main, pre-existing); VERSION 0.9.1 -> 0.9.2, test/version-bump.sh 'VERSION-BUMP PASS'; quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 1 -> 12 tol 15, function_length_mean 1 -> 3.2 tol 5, duplicate_blocks 0 -> 0 tol 0); check-doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; chief lint 3 tasklists clean.
